Registry sources preserve their copyright notices; license files come from

AppContext appends adapters in actual initial-tree completion order. Pending
completion and concurrent creation can differ from ID order. adapter_index now
returns Option<usize> from linear position, retaining append/desktop-child
order. Removal and the two native index/cache callers use that actual position.
No storage, field, retained tree/cache, synchronization primitive or allocation
was added. Lookup costs O(number of windows), without a sorted-ID premise.

Tests use actual Adapter/PlatformRoot to prove parent/cache indices and removal
releasing the native tree for IDs9,3,7. The Unix protocol fixture additionally
forces reverse Pending completion, concurrent public Adapter creation,
reactivation, tagged removal preserving survivor order, and complete destroy.
The registry control fails the parent-index and retained-child assertions.
This is correctness evidence and contains no byte/RSS/startup improvement claim.
See ../accesskit_unix/GPUI-PATCHES.md and ../../evidence/accesskit-lifecycle.

Close-time cleanup reuses normal Defunct/cache removal/interface removal in
current filtered-tree postorder, including the root independently of role.
The existing unconditional root ChildRemoved occurs once, and the tree guard
ends before AppContext removal. No retained ledger or fields are added. The
real Unix two-window protocol fails on the original retained interfaces and
passes after cleanup, including two actual client-cache removal signals and a
surviving action. Exact role/filter/order tests and composed GPUI native gates
are recorded at ../../evidence/accesskit-close. Net vendor production change
is ten non-test/non-comment lines; close costs three terminal messages per
exposed node, plus the existing root notification. No RSS/startup claim.
